subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: Should core `openclaw backup create` add native large-state scope controls/default exclusions, and if so which state classes must remain protected by default?
rationale: The remaining fix changes a shipped recovery command and can intentionally omit state from backups, so automation cannot choose the durable-state boundary or security posture from source inspection alone.

options.title: Review and narrow the linked PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 as the candidate path, but require conflict resolution, real large-install proof, and explicit protected-state/security review before merge.

options.title: Core minimal warning only
options.body: Keep full backups as the default and add only size/progress/error surfacing while leaving targeted backup selection to plugins or future work.

options.title: Defer native scope to ClawHub
options.body: Document ClawHub package approaches such as `keepmyclaw` for selective backup and close the core feature direction only if maintainers decide native scope controls are out of core.

recommendation.title: Review and narrow the linked PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 as the candidate path, but require conflict resolution, real large-install proof, and explicit protected-state/security review before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main backup hardening and docs history make this the best available routing candidate for the product boundary decision.
